Proof of Cigler’s conjecture on qq-Hoggatt numbers

Shane Chern S. ChernFakultät für Mathematik, Universität Wien, Oskar-Morgenstern-Platz 1, Wien 1090, Austria Email address: chenxiaohang92@gmail.com, xiaohangc92@univie.ac.at and Wenle Shi W. ShiSchool of Mathematical Sciences, Dalian University of Technology, Dalian 116024, P.R. China Email address: shi-wenle@hotmail.com
Abstract.

We prove the nonnegativity and palindromicity of a family of polynomials arising from qq-Hoggatt numbers. The nonnegativity is derived from Stanley’s (P,ω)(P,\omega)-partition theory through a standard Young tableau formula, while the palindromicity is proved by an involution on rectangular standard Young tableaux. Our result confirms a conjecture of Cigler.

Key words and phrases: 
qq-Hoggatt number, nonnegativity, palindromicity, standard Young tableau.
2020 Mathematics Subject Classification
05A19, 05A15, 05E05, 11B65.

1. Introduction

A polynomial p⁡(x)p(x) is palindromic if the sequence of its coefficients reads the same forwards from the lowest power to the highest as it does backwards. In other words, p⁡(x)p(x) satisfies the condition

p⁡(x)=xN​p​(x−1),\displaystyle p(x)=x^{N}p(x^{-1}),

where NN is the sum of the lowest and highest exponents. A classic example of palindromic polynomials is the qq-binomial coefficient

[nk]q:={(q,q)n(q,q)k​(q,q)n−k,if 0≤k≤n,0,otherwise,\displaystyle{\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{n}{k}}_{q}:=\begin{cases}\dfrac{(q;q)_{n}}{(q;q)_{k}(q;q)_{n-k}},&\text{if $0\leq k\leq n$},\\[10.0pt] 0,&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}

where the qq-Pochhammer symbol is defined by

(a,q)m\displaystyle(a;q)_{m} :=∏j=0m−1(1−a​qj).\displaystyle:=\prod_{j=0}^{m-1}(1-aq^{j}).

As a polynomial in qq, the qq-binomial coefficient [nk]q{\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{n}{k}}_{q} has lowest exponent 00 and highest exponent k⁡(n−k)k(n-k), while it is a standard result [4, p. 353, eq. (I.47)] that

[nk]q−1=qk⁡(k−n)​[nk]q.\displaystyle{\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{n}{k}}_{q^{-1}}=q^{k(k-n)}{\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{n}{k}}_{q}.

In [2], Cigler introduced a qq-analog of Hoggatt numbers originating from [3], and conjectured a palindromic property for a relevant series. Let

⟨n⟩q(d):=[n+d−1d]q,⟨n⟩q(d)!:=∏j=1n⟨j⟩q(d).\displaystyle\langle n\rangle_{q}^{(d)}:={\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{n+d-1}{d}}_{q},\qquad\qquad\langle n\rangle_{q}^{(d)}!:=\prod_{j=1}^{n}\langle j\rangle_{q}^{(d)}.

Cigler’s qq-Hoggatt numbers are defined by

(1.1) ⟨nk⟩q(d):=⟨n⟩q(d)!⟨k⟩q(d)!​⟨n−k⟩q(d)!=∏j=0d−1[n+jk]q[k+jk]q.\displaystyle{\genfrac{}{}{0.0pt}{}{n}{k}}_{q}^{(d)}:=\frac{\langle n\rangle_{q}^{(d)}!}{\langle k\rangle_{q}^{(d)}!\langle n-k\rangle_{q}^{(d)}!}=\prod_{j=0}^{d-1}\frac{{\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{n+j}{k}}_{q}}{{\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{k+j}{k}}_{q}}.

For d=1d=1, 22, and 33, the qq-Hoggatt numbers ⟨nk⟩q(d){\genfrac{}{}{0.0pt}{}{n}{k}}_{q}^{(d)} reduce to the qq-binomial coefficients, the qq-Narayana numbers, and the qq-Baxter numbers, respectively.

Cigler [2, Conjecture 10] proposed the following conjecture on qq-Hoggatt numbers.

Cigler’s Conjecture.

Let dd and kk be any positive integers. The series

(1.2) Ck(d)​(x,q):=(x,q)k​d+1​∑n≥0⟨n+kk⟩q(d)​xn\displaystyle C_{k}^{(d)}(x,q):=(x;q)_{kd+1}\sum_{n\geq 0}{\genfrac{}{}{0.0pt}{}{n+k}{k}}_{q}^{(d)}x^{n}

is a bivariate polynomial in xx and qq with nonnegative coefficients, with the highest exponent of xx being (k−1)​(d−1)(k-1)(d-1). Writing

Ck(d)​(x,q)=:∑j=0(k−1)​(d−1)ck,j(d)​(q)​xj,\displaystyle C_{k}^{(d)}(x,q)=:\sum_{j=0}^{(k-1)(d-1)}c_{k,j}^{(d)}(q)x^{j},

it is further true that ck,j(d)​(q)c_{k,j}^{(d)}(q) is palindromic in qq for every kk.

The main purpose of this note is to prove Cigler’s conjecture by means of Stanley’s (P,ω)(P,\omega)-partition theory [5, 6, 7].

Recall that an integer partition λ\lambda is a weakly decreasing sequence of positive integers known as parts; the size of this partition, denoted by |λ||\lambda|, is the sum of all its parts. We may visually represent a partition λ=(λ1,λ2,…,λl)\lambda=(\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2},\ldots,\lambda_{l}) by its Young diagram, which is depicted by boxes placed in rows such that there are λi\lambda_{i} boxes in the ii-th row.

Let λ\lambda be a fixed partition. A standard Young tableau of shape λ\lambda is a filling TT of the boxes in the Young diagram of λ\lambda with 1,2,…,|λ|1,2,\ldots,|\lambda|, each used exactly once, such that the entries are strictly increasing along rows and down columns. Let SYT⁡(λ)\operatorname{SYT}(\lambda) denote the set of such tableaux.

For T∈SYT⁡(λ)T\in\operatorname{SYT}(\lambda) and 1≤i≤|λ|1\leq i\leq|\lambda|, let

ρi=(ri,si):=T−1​(i)\displaystyle\rho_{i}=(r_{i},s_{i}):=T^{-1}(i)

denote the box occupied by ii in TT. Define the descent set

Des(T):={i:1≤i≤|λ|−1,ri+1>ri}.\displaystyle\operatorname{Des}(T):=\{i:1\leq i\leq|\lambda|-1,\ r_{i+1}>r_{i}\}.

We require the descent statistic

des⁡(T):=|Des⁡(T)|,\displaystyle\operatorname{des}(T):=|\operatorname{Des}(T)|,

and the comajor index statistic

comaj⁡(T):=∑i∈Des⁡(T)(|λ|−i).\displaystyle\operatorname{comaj}(T):=\sum_{i\in\operatorname{Des}(T)}(|\lambda|-i).

Our main result is to express Cigler’s series Ck(d)​(x,q)C_{k}^{(d)}(x,q) as the generating function for certain standard Young tableaux of rectangular shapes, thereby indicating Cigler’s conjecture. To start with, we let

(kd):=(k,k,…,k⏟d parts),\displaystyle(k^{d}):=(\underbrace{k,k,\ldots,k}_{\text{$d$ parts}}),

the partition into dd parts of size kk. Its Young diagram has a rectangular shape with dd rows and kk columns.

Theorem 1.1.

For every positive integers dd and kk,

(1.3) (x,q)k​d+1​∑n≥0⟨n+kk⟩q(d)​xn=∑T∈SYT⁡(kd)qcomaj⁡(T)−k​(d2)​xdes⁡(T)−(d−1).\displaystyle(x;q)_{kd+1}\sum_{n\geq 0}{\genfrac{}{}{0.0pt}{}{n+k}{k}}_{q}^{(d)}x^{n}=\sum_{T\in\operatorname{SYT}(k^{d})}q^{\operatorname{comaj}(T)-k\binom{d}{2}}x^{\operatorname{des}(T)-(d-1)}.

Moreover, Cigler’s conjecture is true. In particular, the coefficients at the lowest and highest powers of xx are respectively

ck,0(d)​(q)\displaystyle c_{k,0}^{(d)}(q) =1,ck,(k−1)​(d−1)(d)​(q)=q2​(k2)​(d2).\displaystyle=1,\qquad\qquad c_{k,(k-1)(d-1)}^{(d)}(q)=q^{2\binom{k}{2}\binom{d}{2}}.

This note is organized as follows. In Section 2, we interpret Cigler’s series Ck(d)​(x,q)C_{k}^{(d)}(x,q) combinatorially by proving (1.3); we also determine the coefficients of the two endpoint powers of xx. Next, in Section 3, we establish the palindromicity for all coefficients ck,j(d)​(q)c_{k,j}^{(d)}(q); our argument is built upon a natural involution on rectangular standard Young tableaux. Finally, we close this paper with further discussions on Fibonacci–Hoggatt numbers and resolve another conjecture of Cigler in Section 4.

2. Main Theorem, Part I: Combinatorics

In this part, we prove (1.3). Our starting point is the following observation.

Lemma 2.1.

For every nonnegative integer nn and every positive integers dd and kk,

(2.1) ⟨n+kk⟩q(d)=∑T∈SYT⁡(kd)qcomaj⁡(T)−k​(d2)​[(n+d−1)−des⁡(T)+k​dk​d]q.\displaystyle{\genfrac{}{}{0.0pt}{}{n+k}{k}}_{q}^{(d)}=\sum_{T\in\operatorname{SYT}(k^{d})}q^{\operatorname{comaj}(T)-k\binom{d}{2}}{\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{(n+d-1)-\des(T)+kd}{kd}}_{q}.
Proof.

We begin with a generic partition λ\lambda and a generic nonnegative integer mm. Note that

∑T∈SYT⁡(λ)qcomaj⁡(T)​[m−des⁡(T)+|λ||λ|]q\displaystyle\sum_{T\in\operatorname{SYT}(\lambda)}q^{\operatorname{comaj}(T)}{\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{m-\des(T)+|\lambda|}{|\lambda|}}_{q}
=∑T∈SYT⁡(λ)qdes⁡(T)⋅|λ|−maj⁡(T)​q(m−des⁡(T))⋅|λ|​[m−des⁡(T)+|λ||λ|]q−1,\displaystyle\qquad=\sum_{T\in\operatorname{SYT}(\lambda)}q^{\operatorname{des}(T)\cdot|\lambda|-\operatorname{maj}(T)}q^{(m-\operatorname{des}(T))\cdot|\lambda|}{\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{m-\des(T)+|\lambda|}{|\lambda|}}_{q^{-1}},

where the major index of TT is given by

maj⁡(T):=∑i∈Des⁡(T)i.\displaystyle\operatorname{maj}(T):=\sum_{i\in\operatorname{Des}(T)}i.

Thus,

∑T∈SYT⁡(λ)qcomaj⁡(T)​[m−des⁡(T)+|λ||λ|]q\displaystyle\sum_{T\in\operatorname{SYT}(\lambda)}q^{\operatorname{comaj}(T)}{\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{m-\des(T)+|\lambda|}{|\lambda|}}_{q}
=qm​|λ|​∑T∈SYT⁡(λ)q−maj⁡(T)​[m−des⁡(T)+|λ||λ|]q−1.\displaystyle\qquad=q^{m|\lambda|}\sum_{T\in\operatorname{SYT}(\lambda)}q^{-\operatorname{maj}(T)}{\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{m-\des(T)+|\lambda|}{|\lambda|}}_{q^{-1}}.

In light of [8, p. 364, Proposition 7.19.12], the sum on the right-hand side of the above can be expressed in terms of a Schur function:

(2.2) ∑T∈SYT⁡(λ)qcomaj⁡(T)​[m−des⁡(T)+|λ||λ|]q=qm​|λ|​sλ​(1,q−1,…,q−m).\displaystyle\sum_{T\in\operatorname{SYT}(\lambda)}q^{\operatorname{comaj}(T)}{\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{m-\des(T)+|\lambda|}{|\lambda|}}_{q}=q^{m|\lambda|}s_{\lambda}(1,q^{-1},\ldots,q^{-m}).

According to the above discussions, we have

RHS⁡(2.1)=qk​d​(n+d−1)−k​(d2)​s(kd)​(1,q−1,…,q−(n+d−1)).\displaystyle\operatorname{RHS}\eqref{eq:gf-middle}=q^{kd(n+d-1)-k\binom{d}{2}}s_{(k^{d})}(1,q^{-1},\ldots,q^{-(n+d-1)}).

Now we recall the principal evaluation of Schur functions [8, p. 374, Theorem 7.21.2] so that

s(kd)​(1,q−1,…,q−(n+d−1))\displaystyle s_{(k^{d})}(1,q^{-1},\ldots,q^{-(n+d-1)}) =q−k​(d2)​∏i=1d∏j=1k1−q−(n+d+j−i)1−q−(k+d−i−j+1)\displaystyle=q^{-k\binom{d}{2}}\prod_{i=1}^{d}\prod_{j=1}^{k}\frac{1-q^{-(n+d+j-i)}}{1-q^{-(k+d-i-j+1)}}
=q−k​(d2)​∏i=1d∏j=1k1−q−(n+i+j−1)1−q−(i+j−1).\displaystyle=q^{-k\binom{d}{2}}\prod_{i=1}^{d}\prod_{j=1}^{k}\frac{1-q^{-(n+i+j-1)}}{1-q^{-(i+j-1)}}.

Therefore,

RHS⁡(2.1)=qk​d​(n+d−1)−2​k​(d2)​∏i=1d∏j=1k1−q−(n+i+j−1)1−q−(i+j−1)=∏i=1d∏j=1k1−qn+i+j−11−qi+j−1.\displaystyle\operatorname{RHS}\eqref{eq:gf-middle}=q^{kd(n+d-1)-2k\binom{d}{2}}\prod_{i=1}^{d}\prod_{j=1}^{k}\frac{1-q^{-(n+i+j-1)}}{1-q^{-(i+j-1)}}=\prod_{i=1}^{d}\prod_{j=1}^{k}\frac{1-q^{n+i+j-1}}{1-q^{i+j-1}}.

Finally, we know from the definition (1.1) that

LHS⁡(2.1)=⟨n+kk⟩q(d)=∏j=0d−1[n+k+jk]q[k+jk]q=∏j=1d∏i=1k1−qn+i+j−11−qi+j−1,\displaystyle\operatorname{LHS}\eqref{eq:gf-middle}={\genfrac{}{}{0.0pt}{}{n+k}{k}}_{q}^{(d)}=\prod_{j=0}^{d-1}\frac{{\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{n+k+j}{k}}_{q}}{{\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{k+j}{k}}_{q}}=\prod_{j=1}^{d}\prod_{i=1}^{k}\frac{1-q^{n+i+j-1}}{1-q^{i+j-1}},

thereby giving the claimed relation (2.1) by interchanging the indices ii and jj. ∎

In view of (2.1), we have

∑n≥0⟨n+kk⟩q(d)​xn=∑T∈SYT⁡(kd)qcomaj⁡(T)−k​(d2)​∑n≥0[(n+d−1)−des⁡(T)+k​dk​d]q​xn.\displaystyle\sum_{n\geq 0}{\genfrac{}{}{0.0pt}{}{n+k}{k}}_{q}^{(d)}x^{n}=\sum_{T\in\operatorname{SYT}(k^{d})}q^{\operatorname{comaj}(T)-k\binom{d}{2}}\sum_{n\geq 0}{\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{(n+d-1)-\des(T)+kd}{kd}}_{q}x^{n}.

To simplify the inner sum on the right-hand side, we need to determine the range of des⁡(T)\operatorname{des}(T).

Lemma 2.2.

For standard Young tableaux T∈SYT⁡(kd)T\in\operatorname{SYT}(k^{d}), we have

(2.3) d−1≤des⁡(T)≤k⁡(d−1).\displaystyle d-1\leq\operatorname{des}(T)\leq k(d-1).

Moreover, both inequalities are attainable, each by a unique standard Young tableau.

Proof.

For the lower bound, we assume that in the standard Young tableau TT, the entries in the first column are u1<u2<⋯<udu_{1}<u_{2}<\cdots<u_{d}. For each ui+1−1u_{i+1}-1 with 1≤i≤d−11\leq i\leq d-1, it is clear that its row index must be smaller than that of ui+1u_{i+1}, thereby implying that ui+1−1u_{i+1}-1 is a descent. Hence,

des⁡(T)≥|{u2−1,u3−1,…,ud−1}|=d−1.\displaystyle\operatorname{des}(T)\geq\big|\{u_{2}-1,u_{3}-1,\ldots,u_{d}-1\}\big|=d-1.

On the other hand, suppose the entries in the last column are u1′<u2′<⋯<ud′u^{\prime}_{1}<u^{\prime}_{2}<\cdots<u^{\prime}_{d}. It is also true that all u1′,…,ud−1′u^{\prime}_{1},\ldots,u^{\prime}_{d-1} are descents. To ensure des⁡(T)=d−1\operatorname{des}(T)=d-1, we must have ui′=ui+1−1u^{\prime}_{i}=u_{i+1}-1 for 1≤i≤d−11\leq i\leq d-1. In this situation, the only possibility is the standard Young tableau T†T^{\dagger} of shape (kd)(k^{d}) in which the entry in the ii-th row and jj-th column is j+(i−1)​kj+(i-1)k.

For the upper bound, we assume that the first row of the standard Young tableau TT is filled with v1<v2<⋯<vkv_{1}<v_{2}<\cdots<v_{k}. For each vj+1−1v_{j+1}-1 with 1≤j≤k−11\leq j\leq k-1, its row index is at least 11, which is never smaller than that of vj+1v_{j+1}. Thus,

des⁡(T)≤|{1,2,…,k​d−1}\{v2−1,v3−1,…,vk−1}|=k⁡(d−1).\displaystyle\operatorname{des}(T)\leq\big|\{1,2,\ldots,kd-1\}\backslash\{v_{2}-1,v_{3}-1,\ldots,v_{k}-1\}\big|=k(d-1).

Suppose further that the entries in the last row are v1′<v2′<⋯<vk′v^{\prime}_{1}<v^{\prime}_{2}<\cdots<v^{\prime}_{k}. It is clear that v1′,…,vk−1′v^{\prime}_{1},\ldots,v^{\prime}_{k-1} are non-descents. Thus, to ensure des⁡(T)=k⁡(d−1)\operatorname{des}(T)=k(d-1), we must have vj′=vj+1−1v^{\prime}_{j}=v_{j+1}-1. Then the only possible standard Young tableau T‡T^{\ddagger} is such that the (i,j)(i,j)-th box is filled with i+(j−1)​di+(j-1)d. ∎

According to (2.3), for every T∈SYT⁡(kd)T\in\operatorname{SYT}(k^{d}),

(d−1)−des⁡(T)≤0.\displaystyle(d-1)-\operatorname{des}(T)\leq 0.

Thus,

∑n≥0[(n+d−1)−des⁡(T)+k​dk​d]q​xn=xdes⁡(T)−(d−1)​∑i≥0[i+k​dk​d]q​xi.\displaystyle\sum_{n\geq 0}{\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{(n+d-1)-\des(T)+kd}{kd}}_{q}x^{n}=x^{\operatorname{des}(T)-(d-1)}\sum_{i\geq 0}{\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{i+kd}{kd}}_{q}x^{i}.

Now we can apply the following evaluation of qq-binomial series [1, p. 36, eq. (3.3.7)]:

∑i≥0[i+jj]q​xi=1(x,q)j+1,\displaystyle\sum_{i\geq 0}{\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{i+j}{j}}_{q}x^{i}=\frac{1}{(x;q)_{j+1}},

from which we get

∑n≥0[(n+d−1)−des⁡(T)+k​dk​d]q​xn=xdes⁡(T)−(d−1)(x,q)k​d+1.\displaystyle\sum_{n\geq 0}{\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{(n+d-1)-\des(T)+kd}{kd}}_{q}x^{n}=\frac{x^{\operatorname{des}(T)-(d-1)}}{(x;q)_{kd+1}}.

Finally, we conclude that

∑n≥0⟨n+kk⟩q(d)​xn=1(x,q)k​d+1​∑T∈SYT⁡(kd)qcomaj⁡(T)−k​(d2)​xdes⁡(T)−(d−1),\displaystyle\sum_{n\geq 0}{\genfrac{}{}{0.0pt}{}{n+k}{k}}_{q}^{(d)}x^{n}=\frac{1}{(x;q)_{kd+1}}\sum_{T\in\operatorname{SYT}(k^{d})}q^{\operatorname{comaj}(T)-k\binom{d}{2}}x^{\operatorname{des}(T)-(d-1)},

thereby producing the desired relation (1.3). In addition, we have the coefficient of the lowest power of xx:

ck,0(d)​(q)=qcomaj⁡(T†)−k​(d2)=1,\displaystyle c_{k,0}^{(d)}(q)=q^{\operatorname{comaj}(T^{\dagger})-k\binom{d}{2}}=1,

while the coefficient of the highest power of xx is

ck,(k−1)​(d−1)(d)​(q)=qcomaj⁡(T‡)−k​(d2)=q2​(k2)​(d2);\displaystyle c_{k,(k-1)(d-1)}^{(d)}(q)=q^{\operatorname{comaj}(T^{\ddagger})-k\binom{d}{2}}=q^{2\binom{k}{2}\binom{d}{2}};

here the standard Young tableaux T†T^{\dagger} and T‡T^{\ddagger} are as in the proof of Lemma 2.2.

3. Main Theorem, Part II: Palindromicity

A direct indication of the relation (1.3) and the bounds (2.3) is that Cigler’s series Ck(d)​(x,q)C_{k}^{(d)}(x,q) is in ℕ​[q,q−1]​[x]\mathbb{N}[q,q^{-1}][x], while the highest exponent of xx is (k−1)​(d−1)(k-1)(d-1). Now we shall show that the coefficients ck,j(d)​(q)c_{k,j}^{(d)}(q) of xjx^{j} in Ck(d)​(x,q)C_{k}^{(d)}(x,q) are indeed polynomials in ℕ⁡[q]\mathbb{N}[q] instead of Laurent polynomials. For this purpose, we have to bound comaj⁡(T)\operatorname{comaj}(T) for standard Young tableaux T∈SYT⁡(kd)T\in\operatorname{SYT}(k^{d}).

Lemma 3.1.

For standard Young tableaux T∈SYT⁡(kd)T\in\operatorname{SYT}(k^{d}), we have

(3.1) comaj⁡(T)≥k​(d2).\displaystyle\operatorname{comaj}(T)\geq k\binom{d}{2}.
Proof.

We rewrite comaj⁡(T)\operatorname{comaj}(T) as

comaj⁡(T)=∑i∈Des⁡(T)(k​d−i)=∑m=1k​d|{l∈Des⁡(T):l<m}|.\displaystyle\operatorname{comaj}(T)=\sum_{i\in\operatorname{Des}(T)}(kd-i)=\sum_{m=1}^{kd}\big|\{l\in\operatorname{Des}(T):l<m\}\big|.

Now we prove that, for each mm, there are at least rm−1r_{m}-1 descents smaller than mm, where mm is placed in the (rm,sm)(r_{m},s_{m})-th box. In the sms_{m}-th cloumn, we assume that the first rmr_{m} entries are u1<u2<⋯<urm=:mu_{1}<u_{2}<\cdots<u_{r_{m}}=:m. It is clear that in each interval {ui,ui+1,…,ui+1−1}\{u_{i},u_{i}+1,\ldots,u_{i+1}-1\} with 1≤i≤rm−11\leq i\leq r_{m}-1, there exists at least one descent lil_{i}. Moreover, li≤ui+1−1≤urm−1<ml_{i}\leq u_{i+1}-1\leq u_{r_{m}}-1<m. Since there are rm−1r_{m}-1 such nonintersecting intervals, we have

|{l∈Des⁡(T):l<m}|≥rm−1.\displaystyle\big|\{l\in\operatorname{Des}(T):l<m\}\big|\geq r_{m}-1.

Finally,

comaj⁡(T)≥∑m=1k​d(rm−1)=k​∑i=1d(i−1)=k​(d2),\displaystyle\operatorname{comaj}(T)\geq\sum_{m=1}^{kd}(r_{m}-1)=k\sum_{i=1}^{d}(i-1)=k\binom{d}{2},

as claimed. ∎

Now we have seen that

Ck(d)​(x,q)∈ℕ⁡[q]​[x].\displaystyle C_{k}^{(d)}(x,q)\in\mathbb{N}[q][x].

Moreover, the coefficients ck,j(d)​(q)c_{k,j}^{(d)}(q) are given by

ck,j(d)​(q)=∑T∈SYT⁡(kd)des⁡(T)=j+d−1qcomaj⁡(T)−k​(d2).\displaystyle c_{k,j}^{(d)}(q)=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}T\in\operatorname{SYT}(k^{d})\\ \operatorname{des}(T)=j+d-1\end{subarray}}q^{\operatorname{comaj}(T)-k\binom{d}{2}}.

To show these coefficients are palindromic, we need the following observation.

Lemma 3.2.

Define a map θ:SYT⁡(kd)→SYT⁡(kd)\theta:\operatorname{SYT}(k^{d})\to\operatorname{SYT}(k^{d}) by

θ⁡(T)​(r,s):=k​d+1−T⁡(d+1−r,k+1−s).\displaystyle\theta(T)(r,s):=kd+1-T(d+1-r,k+1-s).

Then θ\theta is an involution. In addition,

(3.2) des⁡(θ⁡(T))=des⁡(T),\displaystyle\operatorname{des}(\theta(T))=\operatorname{des}(T),

and

(3.3) comaj⁡(θ⁡(T))=k​d​des⁡(T)−comaj⁡(T).\displaystyle\operatorname{comaj}(\theta(T))=kd\operatorname{des}(T)-\operatorname{comaj}(T).
Proof.

It is a direct verification that θ\theta is an involution on SYT⁡(kd)\operatorname{SYT}(k^{d}). Now we check the two relations on statistics. First,

Des⁡(θ⁡(T))={k​d−i:i∈Des⁡(T)},\displaystyle\operatorname{Des}(\theta(T))=\{kd-i:i\in\operatorname{Des}(T)\},

so that (3.2) holds. Next,

comaj⁡(θ⁡(T))=∑i′∈Des⁡(θ⁡(T))(k​d−i′)=∑i∈Des⁡(T)i,\displaystyle\operatorname{comaj}(\theta(T))=\sum_{i^{\prime}\in\operatorname{Des}(\theta(T))}(kd-i^{\prime})=\sum_{i\in\operatorname{Des}(T)}i,

thereby leading us to (3.3). ∎

Note that the map θ\theta, if restricted to the subset of standard Young tableaux

{T∈SYT⁡(kd):des⁡(T)=j+d−1},\displaystyle\{T\in\operatorname{SYT}(k^{d}):\operatorname{des}(T)=j+d-1\},

is still an involution. Moreover,

(comaj⁡(T)−k​(d2))+(comaj⁡(θ⁡(T))−k​(d2))=k​d​(j+d−1)−2​k​(d2)=k​d​j,\displaystyle\left(\operatorname{comaj}(T)-k\binom{d}{2}\right)+\left(\operatorname{comaj}(\theta(T))-k\binom{d}{2}\right)=kd(j+d-1)-2k\binom{d}{2}=kdj,

which is independent of TT. These facts tell us that in ck,j(d)​(q)c_{k,j}^{(d)}(q), the sum of the lowest and highest exponents of qq is k​d​jkdj. Also, by pairing TT and θ⁡(T)\theta(T), we have

ck,j(d)​(q)=qk​d​j​ck,j(d)​(q−1),\displaystyle c_{k,j}^{(d)}(q)=q^{kdj}c_{k,j}^{(d)}(q^{-1}),

and hence conclude the palindromicity.

4. Closing remarks

In [2], Cigler also considered a family of Fibonacci–Hoggatt numbers. For nonzero numbers aa and bb, let (Fa,b​(n))n≥0(F_{a,b}(n))_{n\geq 0} be a sequence defined by the recurrence

Fa,b​(n)=a​Fa,b​(n−1)+b​Fa,b​(n−2),\displaystyle F_{a,b}(n)=aF_{a,b}(n-1)+bF_{a,b}(n-2),

together with the initial values Fa,b​(0)=0F_{a,b}(0)=0 and Fa,b​(1)=1F_{a,b}(1)=1. When a=b=1a=b=1, the sequence reduces to the conventional Fibonacci numbers.

In analogy to (1.1), define the Fibonacci–Hoggatt numbers by

⟨nk⟩Fa,b(d):=⟨n⟩Fa,b(d)!⟨k⟩Fa,b(d)!​⟨n−k⟩Fa,b(d)!=∏j=0d−1[n+jk]Fa,b[k+jk]Fa,b,\displaystyle{\genfrac{}{}{0.0pt}{}{n}{k}}_{F_{a,b}}^{(d)}:=\frac{\langle n\rangle_{F_{a,b}}^{(d)}!}{\langle k\rangle_{F_{a,b}}^{(d)}!\langle n-k\rangle_{F_{a,b}}^{(d)}!}=\prod_{j=0}^{d-1}\frac{{\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{n+j}{k}}_{F_{a,b}}}{{\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{k+j}{k}}_{F_{a,b}}},

where

⟨n⟩Fa,b(d):=[n+d−1d]Fa,b,⟨n⟩Fa,b(d)!:=∏j=1n⟨j⟩Fa,b(d),\displaystyle\langle n\rangle_{F_{a,b}}^{(d)}:={\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{n+d-1}{d}}_{F_{a,b}},\qquad\qquad\langle n\rangle_{F_{a,b}}^{(d)}!:=\prod_{j=1}^{n}\langle j\rangle_{F_{a,b}}^{(d)},

with

[nk]Fa,b:={∏j=0k−1Fa,b​(n−j)Fa,b​(k−j),if 0≤k≤n,0,otherwise.\displaystyle{\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{n}{k}}_{F_{a,b}}:=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\frac{F_{a,b}(n-j)}{F_{a,b}(k-j)},&\text{if $0\leq k\leq n$},\\[10.0pt] 0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}

Note that the numbers Fa,b​(n)F_{a,b}(n) can be expressed by Binet’s formula:

Fa,b​(n)=αn−βnα−β,\displaystyle F_{a,b}(n)=\frac{\alpha^{n}-\beta^{n}}{\alpha-\beta},

where

α:=a+a2+4​b2,β:=a−a2+4​b2.\displaystyle\alpha:=\frac{a+\sqrt{a^{2}+4b}}{2},\qquad\qquad\beta:=\frac{a-\sqrt{a^{2}+4b}}{2}.

Putting

q:=βα,\displaystyle q:=\frac{\beta}{\alpha},

and noting that α​β=−b\alpha\beta=-b, we have

Fa,b​(n)=(−bq)n−12​1−qn1−q,\displaystyle F_{a,b}(n)=\left(-\frac{b}{q}\right)^{\frac{n-1}{2}}\frac{1-q^{n}}{1-q},

so that

[nk]Fa,b=(−qb)k⁡(k−n)2​[nk]q.\displaystyle{\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{n}{k}}_{F_{a,b}}=\left(-\frac{q}{b}\right)^{\frac{k(k-n)}{2}}{\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{n}{k}}_{q}.

In [2], Cigler considered the following series

(4.1) Gk,Fa,b(d)​(x):=(∑m=0k​d+1(−1)(m+12)​b(m2)​[k​d+1m]Fa,b​xm)​(∑n≥0⟨n+kk⟩Fa,b(d)​xn).\displaystyle G_{k,F_{a,b}}^{(d)}(x):=\left(\sum_{m=0}^{kd+1}(-1)^{\binom{m+1}{2}}b^{\binom{m}{2}}{\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{kd+1}{m}}_{F_{a,b}}x^{m}\right)\left(\sum_{n\geq 0}{\genfrac{}{}{0.0pt}{}{n+k}{k}}_{F_{a,b}}^{(d)}x^{n}\right).

If we put

y:=(−bq)k​d2​x,\displaystyle y:=\left(-\frac{b}{q}\right)^{\frac{kd}{2}}x,

it follows from a direct computation that

Gk,Fa,b(d)​(x)=(y,q)k​d+1​∑n≥0⟨n+kk⟩q(d)​yn,\displaystyle G_{k,F_{a,b}}^{(d)}(x)=(y;q)_{kd+1}\sum_{n\geq 0}{\genfrac{}{}{0.0pt}{}{n+k}{k}}_{q}^{(d)}y^{n},

where we have applied the following evaluation [1, p. 36, eq. (3.3.6)] to the first sum in (4.1):

∑i=0j[ji]q​(−1)i​zi​q(i2)=(z,q)j.\displaystyle\sum_{i=0}^{j}{\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{j}{i}}_{q}(-1)^{i}z^{i}q^{\binom{i}{2}}=(z;q)_{j}.

Note that yy and xx only differ by a scalar. By virtue of Theorem 1.1, we may immediately confirm the following conjecture of Cigler [2, Conjecture 18], which also reduces to [2, Conjecture 14] at the a=b=1a=b=1 specialization.

Theorem 4.1.

Gk,Fa,b(d)​(x)G_{k,F_{a,b}}^{(d)}(x) is a polynomial in xx of degree (k−1)​(d−1)(k-1)(d-1) with constant term being 11 and the coefficient of the highest power of xx being b2​(k2)​(d2)b^{2\binom{k}{2}\binom{d}{2}}.
